verdict.rationale: Statsig's docs describe environment-tier isolation. SDKs evaluate gates, configs, and experiments differently in development or staging versus production, environment-specific SDK keys decide which rule sets download, and dev/staging/prod data is kept separate. This covers both independent per-environment flag states and scoped keys. Target apps add further key scoping within a project. Missing for 10: detailed docs on configuring per-environment rules in the console or API, any evidence about custom environment tiers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage separate environments (dev/staging/prod) with independent flag states and scoped SDK keys

citations.quote: evaluate feature gates, dynamic configs, and experiments differently in non-production environments like development or staging
environment-specific SDK keys determining which rule sets download and separated development/staging/production data
Specifying a target app for your client key and linking only client-specific configs to it keeps those configs from being visible.
